newsitem.title: INDIA: India truck owners threaten nationwide strike.
newsitem.headline: India truck owners threaten nationwide strike.

text.p: Indian truck owners threatened on Wednesday to stage a nationwide strike over a proposed new tax and a plan by state-owned insurance firms to raise premiums.
The All India Motor Transport Congress (AIMTC) said delivery of goods through trucks and tankers would be suspended from April 1 unless its demands were met.
The congress represents owners of some two million heavy trucks, one million light and medium-weight trucks and some 60,000 booking and delivery companies. Its members represent 560 unions.

"The road freight services, including trucks, mini trucks, tankers, trailers, and booking and delivery of goods by transport companies shall stop indefinitely from April 1," the AIMTC said in a statement.
Spokesman S.P. Singh said the congress would try to reach a negotiated settlement with the federal government but that time was running out.

The AIMTC objected to a five percent service tax on road transport which Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed in the federal budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year beginning on April 1. A vote on the tax is expected in late April.
It also denounced a decision by state-owned insurance companies which it said would raise transport insurance premiums by between 300 and 400 percent.
The road transport operators said that if "adequate and appropriate" remedies were not provided by the government, they would suspend all their services. It did not elaborate.
Singh said the last time truck owners went on strike was in 1993 when transport of goods was halted for 13 days.
